name: Azure AD / Entra ID Hunt
author: Cloud Identity Team
prerequisites: Global Reader or Security Reader Entra ID role assigned to hunt account
Azure AD Sign-in logs retained for 30+ days (requires P1/P2 license)
Microsoft Defender for Identity or Sentinel workspace access
required_tools: PowerShell Az and AzureAD / Microsoft.Graph modules
MFASweep or AADInternals (for authorized assessment use)

hunt_actions.title: MFA Bypass and Authentication Attack Detection
actions: Hunt MFA fatigue (push bombing): Sentinel KQL: `SigninLogs | where ResultType == '50076' | summarize PushCount=count(), TimeRange=max(TimeGenerated)-min(TimeGenerated) by UserPrincipalName, IPAddress, bin(TimeGenerated,1h) | where PushCount > 10 | order by PushCount desc` — 50076 is the result code for MFA required but not satisfied.

Identify legacy authentication protocol usage: `SigninLogs | where ClientAppUsed in ('Exchange ActiveSync','IMAP4','POP3','SMTP','Mapi','AutoDiscover','Other clients') | summarize count() by UserPrincipalName, ClientAppUsed, IPAddress | order by count_ desc` — legacy auth bypasses modern MFA; any result should be investigated and blocked.

Detect adversary-in-the-middle / token theft indicators: `SigninLogs | where isnotempty(TokenProtectionStatus) and TokenProtectionStatus == 'unbound' | where AppId !in ('<approved_app_ids>') | project TimeGenerated, UserPrincipalName, IPAddress, Location, AppDisplayName, UserAgent` — unbound tokens on sensitive apps indicate potential AiTM phishing.

Review Conditional Access policy exclusions: In Entra portal navigate to Protection > Conditional Access > Policies > select each policy > Conditions > Users > Excluded Users. Export via Graph: `Connect-MgGraph -Scopes 'Policy.Read.All'; Get-MgIdentityConditionalAccessPolicy | ForEach { $_.Conditions.Users.ExcludeUsers }` — any named exclusion from MFA policies must be reviewed.

hunt_actions.title: Privileged Role Abuse
actions: Audit all privileged role assignments: `Connect-MgGraph -Scopes 'RoleManagement.Read.Directory'; Get-MgDirectoryRole | ForEach { $role=$_; Get-MgDirectoryRoleMember -DirectoryRoleId $role.Id | Select @{n='Role';e={$role.DisplayName}}, @{n='Member';e={$_.AdditionalProperties.userPrincipalName}} } | Export-Csv privileged_roles.csv` — compare against approved role assignment list.

Detect PIM role activations outside business hours: Sentinel KQL: `AuditLogs | where OperationName == 'Add member to role completed (PIM activation)' | extend UPN=tostring(TargetResources[0].userPrincipalName), Role=tostring(TargetResources[0].displayName) | where hourofday(TimeGenerated) !between (8 .. 18) or dayofweek(TimeGenerated) in (0d, 6d) | project TimeGenerated, UPN, Role, InitiatedBy`

Hunt for guest accounts with privileged role assignments: `Get-MgDirectoryRole | ForEach { $role=$_; Get-MgDirectoryRoleMember -DirectoryRoleId $role.Id } | Where-Object { $_.AdditionalProperties.userType -eq 'Guest' } | Select AdditionalProperties` — guests should never hold privileged directory roles.

Identify service principals with owner rights on sensitive apps: `Get-MgApplication | ForEach { $app=$_; Get-MgApplicationOwner -ApplicationId $app.Id | Select @{n='App';e={$app.DisplayName}}, @{n='Owner';e={$_.AdditionalProperties.userPrincipalName}} }` — compare against approved application ownership registry.

hunt_actions.title: Application and OAuth Abuse
actions: Hunt for OAuth consent grants to unverified applications: `Get-MgOauth2PermissionGrant -All | Where-Object { $_.ConsentType -eq 'Principal' } | Select ClientId, Scope, PrincipalId | Export-Csv oauth_grants.csv` — then cross-reference ClientId against list of Microsoft-verified publishers in Entra portal under App Registrations > All Applications > filter Verified.

Detect application impersonation permissions granted without admin review: `Get-MgServicePrincipal -All | ForEach { Get-MgServicePrincipalAppRoleAssignment -ServicePrincipalId $_.Id } | Where-Object { $_.PrincipalType -eq 'ServicePrincipal' } | Select PrincipalId, ResourceId, AppRoleId | Export-Csv sp_approle_assignments.csv` — any Mail.ReadWrite, Files.ReadWrite.All, or .FullControl grants without documented approval are high-priority findings.

Identify high-privilege service principal credential additions: Sentinel KQL: `AuditLogs | where OperationName in ('Add service principal credentials','Update application - Certificates and secrets management') | extend SPName=tostring(TargetResources[0].displayName) | project TimeGenerated, SPName, InitiatedBy.user.userPrincipalName, OperationName` — correlate with known key rotation schedules.

questions: Is Microsoft Defender for Identity deployed and configured to send signals to Microsoft Sentinel or Defender XDR for correlation and alerting?
Are Azure AD sign-in logs and audit logs retained for a minimum of 90 days (requires Entra ID P1/P2 or Sentinel ingestion), and is retention verified?
Is Privileged Identity Management (PIM) enforced for all privileged directory roles (Global Admin, Privileged Role Admin, Security Admin, etc.) with just-in-time activation and approval workflow?
Are legacy authentication protocols blocked organization-wide via a Conditional Access policy, and has this been verified with sign-in log analysis for any bypass attempts?

Is multi-factor authentication enforced for all users — including service accounts where technically feasible — via Conditional Access, and are there any named account or group exclusions documented and formally risk-accepted?
Are guest user permissions restricted at the tenant level to prevent enumeration of directory objects (Tenant Settings > External Collaboration Settings > Guest User Access Restriction)?
Is the total count of Global Administrator accounts minimized to five or fewer, with each account formally justified, individually owned, and subject to quarterly access review?
Are app registrations and enterprise applications subject to a formal periodic review process (at least annually), and is there a designated application owner accountable for each registration?
